newsitem.title: USA: Herman to meet Lott in bid to rescue nomination.
newsitem.headline: Herman to meet Lott in bid to rescue nomination.

text.p: President Clinton's embattled Labour Secretary nominee Alexis Herman will meet Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott Friday in an effort to rescue her nomination.

A White House spokesman, Joe Lockhart, said Thursday that Herman would meet Lott sometime during the day Friday in Lott's Capitol Hill office. Her Senate confirmation hearing has been delayed until questions about her are answered.

"She hopes to lay out some of the goals she has for secretary of labour and where she wants to take the department over the next four years," Lockhart said, adding,"It's an opportunity to answer some of the questions that have been raised in the press."

Lott of Mississippi has said Herman might have come close to violating the law in her work as director of the White House office of public liaison. The Hatch Act bars government officials from partisan activities.

During Clinton's re-election campaign, Herman authored a report that said African American contributors should receive personal attention by the Democratic National Committee beyond personal invitations to White House affairs.

In addition, Herman was responsible for adding the name of the Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig to the guest list of a White House coffee with Clinton attended by Democratic Party fund-raisers and top banking officials. White House officials said Ludwig's name was added based on a misunderstanding.

Clinton said Tuesday that Ludwig should not have been included in the May meeting after critics said it was inappropriate to mix party fund-raisers with a federal regulator who holds much power over the potential donors.

Lott told reporters Thursday that he had supported Herman's initial selection for the labour position but now felt "we cannot just lightly dismiss the situation or the circumstances that were going on there at the White House during the campaign and what her involvement was."
"We may find that, you know, there's no major problem there," he said, but added that questions would have to be asked.

Lott also accused White House spokesman Mike McCurry of taking a "gratuitous slap" by questioning Lott's motivation. McCurry said Wednesday he could not believe Lott would question Herman's qualifications because she attempted to encourage blacks to participate in politics.
McCurry said Thursday he was taken out of context and had called Lott to explain it.
"That is the kind of statement, though, that I'm not going to put up with out of the White House," Lott said.
